test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: maths
question: If x⁴ + y⁴ + x²y² = 17(1)/(16) and x² – xy + y² = 5(1)/(4), then one of the values of (x – y) is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identity: x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴ = (x² + xy + y²)(x² − xy + y²)

x² + xy + y² = (273/16) ÷ (21/4) = 13/4

Subtracting factors: 2xy = (x² + xy + y²) − (x² − xy + y²) = 13/4 − 21/4 = −2 ⇒ xy = −1

(x − y)² = (x² − xy + y²) − xy = 21/4 − (−1) = 25/4

Taking square root: x − y = √(25/4) = 5/2

**∴ The correct answer is 5/2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

x⁴ + y⁴ + x²y² = 17 1/16 = 273/16

x² − xy + y² = 5 1/4 = 21/4

Formula used: x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴ = (x² + xy + y²)(x² − xy + y²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/985120b103949ff051ac6a26489a4ea3397e2ffccb484741c52c0370a3dcae5e.png] 

⇒ Let (x² + xy + y²) = A and (x² − xy + y²) = B

⇒ A × B = 273/16

⇒ A × (21/4) = 273/16

⇒ A = (273/16) × (4/21) = 13/4

⇒ A − B = (x² + xy + y²) − (x² − xy + y²) = 2xy

⇒ 2xy = 13/4 − 21/4 = −8/4 = −2

⇒ xy = −1

⇒ (x − y)² = x² − 2xy + y² = (x² − xy + y²) − xy

⇒ (x − y)² = 21/4 − (−1) = 21/4 + 1 = 25/4

⇒ x − y = √(25/4) = 5/2

**∴ The correct answer is 5/2.**

**__Additional Information__**

The Sophie Germain Variant Identity

The expression x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴ can always be factored into (x² + xy + y²) and (x² − xy + y²) by adding and subtracting x²y².

Relationship between components

x² + y² = ½ [(x² + xy + y²) + (x² − xy + y²)] and xy = ½ [(x² + xy + y²) − (x² − xy + y²)].

Square of Difference

(x − y)² = (x² − xy + y²) − xy, which provides a direct route once xy and the factor are known.</p
